I made both edits in `src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py`. `Scaffold.patch` now calls `self.route(rule, methods=["PATCH"], **options)`, and the new `options_route` method sits directly after it. I didn't run the tests.

After the change, five methods call `_method_route` directly. All of them are in `Scaffold`:
- `get`, `post`, `put` and `delete`, which were already calling it.
- `options_route`, the new method.

`patch` no longer calls it. I confirmed this list with a grep of `src/flask/`.

One side effect: `_method_route` is what raises a `TypeError` when someone passes `methods=` to one of these shortcuts. Because `patch` now skips it, calling `patch(..., methods=[...])` no longer gives that clear error. It will probably fail with a less helpful "multiple values for keyword argument 'methods'" error instead.
